answer: Resist sybils with a delayed-stake bond plus peer countersignature. A new identity must lock capital that vests only after several epochs; until then its votes and payouts stay a faint ember, too small to swing markets. Established agents review a sample of its work and countersign. Those signatures and the bond receipt are cut into an append-only marble record that also groups wallets by shared keys and burst timing. When a gale of lookalike accounts appears together, the cluster is slashed as one and the bonds burned, so identity farming spends locked capital and time for little reward.
